text: There have been remarkable developments in the Middle East over the past 24 hours as part of Operation Epic Fury, a joint attack on Iran by the United States and Israel.
Iranian state media has confirmed the death of Iran's head of state, a 86-year-old Supreme Leader Ayatollah Homenay, a man that President Trump has called one of the most evil people in history.
Iranian media reports that Homenay's daughter and grandchild were also killed in the strikes.
This is an image of the Ayatollah's compound that was destroyed in an aerial attack.
Also confirmed dead, the commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the secretary of the Iranian Defense Council, and the chief of the country's armed forces.
President Trump and a pre-recorded announcement of the attack endorsed regime change in the country, telling Iranians to rise up and take control of their government.
Iranian officials have pledged a massive retaliation with, quote, no red lines against American and Israeli targets in the region.
Casualty counts include at least one person in Israel, one person in Dubai, and four people in Syria reportedly killed in Iranian attacks.
In Iran, the Iranian Red Crescent says more than 200 people have been killed and around 700 injured.
Central Command reports that there have been no U.S.
Navy ships have been struck by Iranian missiles or live fire, and that damage to U.S.
installations in the region is minimal and has not impacted operations.
Iran has been able to launch retaliatory strikes with some success, including a recent barrage against U.S.
But right now, it's not clear how much more firepower Iran has in its arsenal.
Also unclear who's even directing Iran's military and security forces right now as we wait for new leadership to emerge.
Here in the U.S., there were celebrations by Iranian Americans in Los Angeles.
